answer.policy_title: Musculoskeletal Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Joint Surgery
criteria_quotes: Knee pain with at least one physical exam finding of a meniscal tear (e.g., joint line tenderness, positive McMurray's test, or Thessaly test).
MRI confirmation of the meniscal pathology demonstrating a tear consistent with the clinical findings.

Failure of conservative management (including physical therapy and/or a structured home exercise program, analgesics/NSAIDs, and activity modification) for at least 6 weeks for acute tears, and up to 12 weeks for chronic or degenerative tears.
Mechanical symptoms (such as locking, catching, or giving-way) may excuse the patient from the conservative management trial if the tear is acute and traumatic.
Absence of moderate to severe osteoarthritis (such as Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) which would make a partial meniscectomy clinically inappropriate.

- In Writing: Mail the written appeal letter and supporting clinical documentation to:
  HMO Nevada Member Services / Appeals Department
  P.O. Box 5747
  Denver, CO 80217-5747
  (Alternative address: HMO Nevada, P.O. Box 17549, Denver, CO 80217-7549)
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The patient can obtain the exact, full verbatim clinical criteria applied to their case by calling the Anthem Member Services number on the back of their insurance card, or by contacting Carelon Medical Benefits Management directly. The ordering provider can also access these guidelines on the Carelon Provider Portal at providerportal.com.
